messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum 25(OH)D concentration was associated with lower depression scores (BDI) in the total sample of young adults.
Sentence: "In this sample (28.2 ± 3.1 years, 52% female, 53% black), serum 25(OH)D concentration was negatively related to BDI, STAI, PSS, total CMHS score, and the majority of CMHS subscale scores (p-values < 0.05)."
Measured as: depression (Beck Depression Inventory, BDI)
Population: 327 black and white young adults (mean age 28.2 years, 52% female, 53% black)
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D concentration (measured, not given)
Comparator: Lower serum 25(OH)D concentrations
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 327
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation did not change mean depressive symptom scores compared with placebo in pregnant women with low vitamin D.
Sentence: "After the intervention, there was no statistically significant difference between the two groups in terms of FBG (P = 0.850), FBI (P = 0.353), HOMA-IR (P = 0.632), mean score of depressive symptoms (P = 0.505), frequency of gestational diabetes (P = 0.187) and frequency of abortion (P = 1.000) and there was only a difference in terms of serum vitamin D level (P = 0.016) and musculoskeletal pain including knee pain (P = 0.025), ankle pain (P < 0.001) and leg pain (P < 0.001)."
Measured as: mean score of depressive symptoms
Population: 88 pregnant women at 8-10 weeks of pregnancy with vitamin D less than 30 ng/ml
Intervention: Vitamin D 4,000 units daily for 18 weeks
Comparator: Placebo tablets
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 88
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is a cross-sectional association of measured serum 25(OH)D with BDI, while Study B is a placebo RCT of supplementation finding no change, so the pair differs in design and exposure type; the disagreement is genuine with design_or_bias as the primary reason.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","comparator"],"detail":"design: cross-sectional association vs randomized placebo-controlled trial; Study A measured level, Study B gave 4,000 IU daily in pregnant women with vitamin D under 30 ng/ml"}
